K's words on the newsletter, verbatim, and how the lead read them.

Fri, Oct 23, 2026: "can i make a monthly newletter be hosted on the site for our leaders to collaborativly edit and it goes out automatically on the same date and time (unless edited) to a list of our members (email list given at first and then all new members get added with an opt-out feature)?"

Tue, Nov 10, 2026: "I am ready whenever you are to look at some custom newletter designs, for the page that hosts their creation and management (what ever that needs to be), and how they look when received by the receipient." Also on Tue, Nov 10: "we have always advertise lca membership as access to this kind of newsletter, so we can use every email we have in the site"; opt-outs are per list, so leaving the newsletter does not stop event mail or a club's mail; LCA admins, the president and a new media manager may write and send it; "we have no physical address and dont want one".

Reading: this is the FIRST round for the newsletter, and K asked for two things: (1) the page on the site where LCA's leaders create and manage the newsletter, whatever that page needs to be, and (2) how the newsletter looks when a person receives it. So each of the four boards is one direction that answers both: a way of making the newsletter, and the email that way of making it produces. They all sit inside the decided look (the kit, the decided header, the decided admin chrome); what differs is the idea of what the newsletter is and how much work it asks of the leaders each month. K is the site's owner; write "K" or "they", never "he" or "his". K picks one, or parts of several, as in every earlier round.
drawExtra: This is round 1 for a new canvas page, "18 · Newsletter". Before drawing, read: the spec file's flow field in full (it holds the moment drawn, the five shared frames, the management facts, the email's footer, the sample issue, the checked weekdays and the open questions); docs/redesign/canvas/boards/Work-J.dc.html (the decided admin home: use its page chrome, cards, status words and density for the creating and managing frames); docs/redesign/canvas/boards/Work-H-2.dc.html (an email being written inside the workspace, for the feel of a composer in this kit); docs/redesign/decided-boards/Nav-Header-Final.dc.html (the signed-in header); docs/redesign/canvas/boards/News-Final.dc.html (dated rows, date tiles, club colour dots, and where the sample issue's facts come from); docs/redesign/decided-boards/Home-Final-Phones.dc.html (phone bezels). Each frame gets a lettered frame label like News-Final's ("A  Creating · the December 2026 issue, Mon, Nov 23, 2026, signed in as the media manager"). The title strip reads "18 · NEWSLETTER · OPTION" and then the option's name; "Built from" names the decided boards used; "Replaces" reads "Nothing yet: first round". Make this option's one idea obvious within two seconds of looking at frame A, and do not borrow the other options' ideas. The email frames must look like real email a person would be glad to get, drawn with the same care as the page.
reviewExtra: List every date on both boards with its weekday and check each against the flow field's checked list (compute any date not on it). List every button and link label and confirm each says what it does or where it goes. Confirm there is no em dash and no en dash in any copy or note (ranges use "to"). Confirm every status is in words. Confirm the editors are shown by role and initials, never by a person's name. Confirm the email footer has the sentence, the three links and the dashed address slot with no address in it, and that Settings shows the mailing address as not set. Confirm the From address is badged as sample. Confirm the partner event never has Register or a count. Confirm the option's send rule is written out in words in frame A or B exactly as its spec gives it. Confirm no trade words (preheader, deliverability, campaign, segment, WYSIWYG). For Newsletter-D only: check every drawn board square by square against the piece list in the spec (every piece on its square, every other square empty, a1 dark, rank 8 at the top) and that this month's answer is printed nowhere.
flow:
SHARED BY ALL FOUR OPTIONS (read this first; every option uses the same sample issue and the same management facts, so K compares the four ideas and not the copy).

WHAT IT IS. LCA's monthly newsletter. Three kinds of people may write and send it: LCA admins, the president and the media manager. They write it together on the site. It goes out by email on the same day and time each month. Every LCA member gets it unless they have unsubscribed.

WHERE THE PAGE LIVES. In the admin area, as its own page named "Newsletter", next to Group email. Use the decided header (signed in, My LCA menu) and the decided admin chrome from Work-J (the admin home K picked), with a crumb line "Admin / Newsletter". Today's Group email page has a subject field, a rich text box (bold, link, lists), "Send a test" to an address, a confirm step and a send history; the newsletter page grows from that, so nothing drawn here should need a tool the site does not have, apart from what the option's own idea adds.

THE MOMENT DRAWN. Mon, Nov 23, 2026 at 2:15 PM. Signed in as the media manager. The first issue, November 2026, went out on Mon, Nov 16, 2026. The December 2026 issue is being written and goes out Tue, Dec 1, 2026 at 8:00 AM Central, in 8 days. The email frames show that December issue as a member receives it on Tue, Dec 1, 2026.

FRAMES, the same five on every option so the boards line up.
- Main board, frame A, "Creating": the Newsletter page at 1440 wide in a browser frame, with the December 2026 issue open for writing. This is the heart of the option. About 1250 tall.
- Main board, frame B, "Managing": the parts of the same page that run the newsletter, drawn as panels or states side by side: the schedule and its send rule, who gets it, the check before it goes, the report on the November issue, past issues, and the newsletter's settings. About 1150 tall.
- Part 2, frame C, "Received on a computer": first the inbox line (sender, subject, the short preview line, the time), then the opened email, a 600 wide message in a plain mail window with the From line, the subject and "Tue, Dec 1, 2026, 8:00 AM". Show the top and the footer in full; a long middle may be cut with a marked "continues" break.
- Part 2, frame D, "Received on a phone": two phones at 390 wide. Phone 1: the top of the email in a mail app. Phone 2: the end of the email with the footer, drawn in the mail app's dark setting so K sees that it holds.
- Part 2, frame E, "The reader's links": the small page a reader lands on after "Unsubscribe from the newsletter": "You will no longer get the LCA newsletter. You will still get emails about tournaments you enter and about your membership." with a button "Undo" and a link "Choose which LCA emails you get". One click, no sign-in, no questions asked.
Lay part 2 out in two columns: the computer view down the left, the phones and frame E down the right.

MANAGING, the same facts on every option (each option arranges them its own way, in frame A's side panel or in frame B):
- Status line: "December 2026 · goes out Tue, Dec 1, 2026 at 8:00 AM Central · in 8 days", with the state in words: Draft, Ready, Held, Sending or Sent.
- Schedule: "The 1st of each month at 8:00 AM Central." Two controls: "Change this month's date or time" and "Hold this issue". K's words: it goes out "on the same date and time (unless edited)".
- The send rule is part of each option (see the option's spec) and is one of the questions K is choosing between.
- People: three editors shown by role with initials in a circle, never by name: "MM Media manager" (you), "PR President", "AD LCA admin". Writing is turn-taking: a part someone is typing in shows "President is editing" and is locked for the others until they leave it; every part shows "Last edited by" a role with a weekday date and a time, and a "History" link with "Restore".
- Goes to: "243 addresses: every LCA member with an email address, one email per address." (the real count on Tue, Nov 10, 2026). Under it, as Sample data: "2 have unsubscribed · 1 address bounced and was removed". A line: "New members are added when they join. Leaving the newsletter does not stop tournament or membership email."
- Check before it goes: "Send a test to me" and a preview switch with three choices in words, "Computer · Phone · Dark". A short checklist in words: "Subject written · Inbox preview line written · 6 links work · 1 photo described". Adding a photo always asks for a one-line description for people who cannot see it.
- Report on November 2026 (Sample data): "Sent to 243 · Delivered 240 · Bounced 3 · Unsubscribed 2 · Spam reports 0", each figure with its word, and the line "LCA does not track who opens an email or what they click."
- Past issues: a short list, newest first: "December 2026 · Draft · goes out Tue, Dec 1, 2026" and "November 2026 · Sent Mon, Nov 16, 2026 · 243 addresses", each with "Open"; sent issues also have "Start a new issue from this one".
- Settings, one compact panel: Sender name "Louisiana Chess Association"; From address newsletter@news.louisianachess.org (badge "Sample data": the exact address is not decided); Replies go to LouisianaChess@gmail.com; Mailing address "Not set. This line is left out of emails until an address is added." with a link "Add an address". Never write an address.

THE EMAIL, the same facts on every option. From "Louisiana Chess Association". Subject "LCA Newsletter · December 2026" unless the option says otherwise. Every email begins with a small link "Read this issue on the site" and ends with the same footer: "You get this newsletter because you are an LCA member." then three links, "Unsubscribe from the newsletter" (one click, stops this list only), "Choose which LCA emails you get", "LCA on Facebook ↗"; then a slot, drawn as a dashed outline with a numbered badge, where LCA's mailing address prints once one is set. The slot is left out of real emails while it is empty. Body text at least 15px, links underlined, every photo with a description, and it must still read with pictures switched off.

THE SAMPLE ISSUE: December 2026, the second issue. Six pieces, in this order unless the option says otherwise. Take names, places and figures from the decided boards (News-Final and Tourn-List-Final) and badge anything invented "Sample data"; one badge per frame is enough, listing what is invented.
1. A note from the president. Three short paragraphs, plain and warm: thanks to the volunteers who ran the State Championship weekend in Sulphur; what is coming in the new year; an ask to renew and to bring one new player to a club night. Signed "LCA President". Do not invent a person's name.
2. Coming up. Three or four events. Ken Ferguson Memorial, Sat to Mon, Jan 16 to 18, 2027, New Orleans, run by Downriver Chess: a partner event, so "Registers on the organizer's site ↗", never Register and never a count. One LCA event with Register (take one from Tourn-List-Final; if its date has passed, give it a Sample date with its weekday). New Orleans Youth Chess: the season began Sat, Nov 14, 2026 and ends with the Grand Prix Final on Sat, May 8, 2027.
3. Results. "Marcus Landry wins the 2026 Louisiana State Championship", 4½ of 5, Sat to Mon, Sep 5 to 7, 2026, Sulphur, 64 players, with one line of section winners as News-Final writes it and a link "Full results".
4. From the clubs. Three short items from News-Final's club rows: Picayune Chess Club's quick-rated nights on first Mondays; Bunkie Chess Club on Tuesdays, 4:00 PM to 6:00 PM at the Bunkie Library, ages 8 to 108, free to join; Baton Rouge Chess Club's Wednesday casual nights. Each with its club colour dot and a link "Club page".
5. Scholastic. Two or three lines for parents on the New Orleans Youth Chess season, with a link "Scholastic".
6. Board business. Two regional representative seats are open (Central Louisiana and Southwest Louisiana); draft minutes of the annual meeting of Sun, Sep 6, 2026 are posted for members' comments; a link "Minutes".

WEEKDAYS (checked; use these, and check any other date you write): Mon, Nov 16, 2026. Sat, Nov 14, 2026. Mon, Nov 23, 2026. Mon, Nov 30, 2026. Tue, Dec 1, 2026. Sat, Dec 12, 2026. Fri, Jan 1, 2027. Sat, Jan 16, 2027 to Mon, Jan 18, 2027. Mon, Feb 1, 2027. Sat, May 8, 2027. Sat, Sep 5, 2026 to Mon, Sep 7, 2026. Sun, Sep 6, 2026.

COPY RULES ON TOP OF THE STANDING ONES. No em dashes and no en dashes anywhere in new copy or notes: write ranges with "to" ("Sat to Mon, Jan 16 to 18, 2027", "4:00 PM to 6:00 PM"). Plain words: a volunteer who has never sent a group email must understand every label, so no trade words (write "inbox preview line", not "preheader"; "bounced", explained once as "the address no longer works"). Every button says what it does. Status always in words beside any colour. Gold is never text on a light ground. Keep every Facebook link the chrome carries and the "300+ members" figure where the chrome carries it.

OPEN FOR K, the same list on every board (put it in the grey note, and badge the first one on the design): (1) the send rule: this option draws its own; the four boards differ on it on purpose. (2) Writing together: drawn as turn-taking, one person in a part at a time, with history; the other choice is everyone typing at once. (3) The day and time. Drawn: the 1st of each month at 8:00 AM Central. (4) Each issue also readable on the site by anyone, behind the email's "Read this issue on the site" link? Drawn: yes. (5) The decided News page has a weekly "News by email" on Mondays at 8:00 AM; does the newsletter replace it or do both run? (6) Opens and clicks are not tracked, as drawn.

boards.title: Newsletter · A · The monthly letter
boards.name: Newsletter-A · The monthly letter
boards.idea: The newsletter is a letter from LCA to its members, and the page where it is made is that letter, open on the screen. One writing column the width of the email, the president's note first, then five short sections under plain headings. What the leaders type is exactly what arrives: mostly words, one photo at most.
boards.differs: The least design and the most voice of the four. Anyone who can write an email can make the whole issue in one sitting, there is nothing to arrange, and it reads well in every mail app. It gives up pictures, layout and anything that fills itself in, so an issue is only as good as what someone writes that month.
boards.keeps: First round, so nothing is carried over from an earlier option. From the decided boards: the signed-in header of Nav-Header-Final, the admin chrome of Work-J, the kit's k-* classes, the cream ground and navy bands, News-Final's dated rows and club colour dots wherever this spec names them, the phone chrome of Home-Final-Phones for the phone bezels, and the board furniture (title strip, legend, grey note).
boards.removes: Nothing: this is the first round for the newsletter. Do not draw the public News page, the preferences page in full, or Group email.
boards.spec:
BOARDS. Newsletter-A.dc.html, 1440 wide, under 3400. Newsletter-A-2.dc.html, 1440 wide, under 3000.

FRAME A, creating. Under the header and the crumb, a page heading "Newsletter" with the status line beside it. The page is two parts. Centre: the letter itself on a white sheet 640px wide, set on the cream ground like a sheet of paper, and typed into directly. At the top of the sheet two labelled fields that are part of the letter: "Subject" (filled: "LCA Newsletter · December 2026") and "Inbox preview line" (filled: "Thank you, Sulphur. Ken Ferguson Memorial in January. Two board seats are open."). Then the letter: "Dear members," and the president's note, then the five sections, each a heading with its text. Show the sheet mid-work: the note and Coming up are written; Results is written; From the clubs carries the banner "President is editing" with a lock and its text greyed; Scholastic is written; Board business is empty and shows the grey prompt "Nothing here yet. A section left empty is left out of the email." Beside each heading, in the margin of the sheet, a small handle to move the section and the line "Last edited by Media manager, Mon, Nov 23, 2026, 1:40 PM · History". A slim writing bar sticks to the top of the sheet with five tools only, in words with icons: Bold, Link, List, Photo, Undo. The one photo (the hall photo) sits after Results with its description shown under it in a field labelled "Describe this photo for people who cannot see it". Right of the sheet, a rail 360px wide: the status and schedule card with the send rule; the People card; the Goes to card; the Check before it goes card with "Send a test to me" and the preview switch. Left of the sheet, a slim outline, "In this letter", listing the six sections with a word for each ("Written", "Being edited", "Empty").

THE SEND RULE for this option: someone must say it is ready. The status card shows a navy button "Mark as ready to send" and the words: "It goes out on Tue, Dec 1, 2026 at 8:00 AM Central once someone marks it ready. If it is not ready the day before, the three editors get a reminder on Mon, Nov 30, 2026 at 8:00 AM. If it is still not ready, it waits and nothing is sent."

FRAME B, managing. Four panels in a row or a two by two grid, each a small state of the same page: (1) the status card in three states side by side, in words: Draft, Ready ("Marked ready by President, Fri, Nov 27, 2026, 4:05 PM · Take it back"), Sent; (2) the report on November 2026; (3) Past issues; (4) Settings, with the mailing address "Not set". Add a fifth small state: the History drawer for one section, with two earlier versions by role and time and "Restore".

FRAME C, received on a computer. The inbox line, then the letter as a mostly text email: a small rook mark and "LCA Newsletter", "December 2026", "Read this issue on the site", then "Dear members," and the note, the sections with their headings and one underlined link each, the one photo, and the shared footer. It should look like a well set letter, not a web page: one column, generous line height, no cards, no buttons.

FRAME D, phones. Phone 1: the top of the letter. Phone 2: the end with the footer, dark.

FRAME E, the shared unsubscribe page.

LEGEND, six notes at most, among them: the sheet is the email, so what is typed is what arrives; one person in a section at a time, with history; an empty section is left out; the send rule (open for K); the address slot in the email footer and its setting; the report without tracking.

boards.title: Newsletter · B · The issue, with a cover
boards.name: Newsletter-B · The issue, with a cover
boards.idea: Every month is an issue with a cover. The leaders build it from numbered pieces: a cover with the month set large, one photo and three cover lines, then a feature and shorter pieces. The page is a builder, with the list of pieces on the left, the piece being written in the middle and the email itself on the right, updating as they type.
boards.differs: The most visual of the four, and the one that feels most like a publication people keep. It asks the most of the leaders: one good photo and three cover lines every month, and a little arranging. A navy cover with the rook mark stands in when there is no photo.
boards.keeps: First round, so nothing is carried over from an earlier option. From the decided boards: the signed-in header of Nav-Header-Final, the admin chrome of Work-J, the kit's k-* classes, the cream ground and navy bands, News-Final's dated rows and club colour dots wherever this spec names them, the phone chrome of Home-Final-Phones for the phone bezels, and the board furniture (title strip, legend, grey note).
boards.removes: Nothing: this is the first round for the newsletter. Do not draw the public News page, the preferences page in full, or Group email.
boards.spec:
BOARDS. Newsletter-B.dc.html, 1440 wide, under 3400. Newsletter-B-2.dc.html, 1440 wide, under 3000.

FRAME A, creating. Under the header and the crumb, a page heading "Newsletter" with the status line, and at the right the buttons "Send a test to me" and "Mark as ready to send". Below, three columns. LEFT, about 300px, "This issue": a numbered list of cards that can be dragged to reorder, each with its kind in words, its title and its state in words. First "Cover" (a small navy thumbnail; "Photo chosen · 3 cover lines"), then "1 Feature: A note from the president" ("Written"), "2 Coming up" ("4 events"), "3 Results" ("Written"), "4 From the clubs" ("President is editing", with a lock), "5 Scholastic" ("Written"), "6 Board business" ("Empty, will be left out"). Under the list a button "Add a piece" with the kinds as a small menu drawn open: Feature, Short piece, Dates, Result, Club news, Photo. MIDDLE, about 520px: the selected card's form. Draw the Cover selected: a photo field showing the hall photo with "Change photo" and the required field "Describe this photo for people who cannot see it"; a line "No photo this month? The cover uses the rook mark on navy."; then "Cover lines, up to three", drawn as a tick list of the pieces' headlines with three ticked and each ticked line editable: "Thank you, Sulphur: the State Championship weekend", "Ken Ferguson Memorial returns, Sat to Mon, Jan 16 to 18, 2027", "Two board seats are open"; then "Subject" and "Inbox preview line" fields. RIGHT, about 480px: "What members will get", the email drawn live at reduced scale with the preview switch (Computer · Phone · Dark) above it, showing the cover and the first pieces, and the part being changed outlined. Under the three columns, a slim strip with the People card and the Goes to card side by side.

THE SEND RULE for this option: someone must say it is ready. Beside "Mark as ready to send": "It goes out on Tue, Dec 1, 2026 at 8:00 AM Central once someone marks it ready. If it is not ready the day before, the three editors get a reminder on Mon, Nov 30, 2026 at 8:00 AM. If it is still not ready, it waits and nothing is sent."

FRAME B, managing. (1) A second state of the middle column: piece 2, Coming up, selected, where events are ticked from the site's calendar (four ticked, weekday dates, the partner event marked "Partner event" with the words "Registers on the organizer's site ↗") and one line of the leaders' own can be added to each. (2) The schedule card with the send rule, in the states Draft, Ready and Sent, in words. (3) The report on November 2026. (4) Past issues drawn as a short shelf of two small covers (December 2026, Draft; November 2026, Sent Mon, Nov 16, 2026) with "Open" and "Start a new issue from this one". (5) Settings, with the mailing address "Not set".

FRAME C, received on a computer. Subject "LCA Newsletter · December 2026 · Thank you, Sulphur". The inbox line, then the email: "Read this issue on the site"; the cover as a navy block with a small label "LCA Newsletter · Issue 2", "December" set very large in white with "2026", the hall photo, and the three numbered cover lines in white; then the whole issue below it in one column, each piece opening with its number in a small navy badge: the feature with a large first paragraph and a pull line set in the heading face, Coming up as dated rows with date tiles, Results as one card with the section winners line and "Full results", From the clubs with colour dots, Scholastic, and the shared footer. Board business is not there, because it was left empty.

FRAME D, phones. Phone 1: the cover filling the first screen of the mail app. Phone 2: the end with the footer, dark. Beside the phones, one small extra: the no-photo cover, navy with the rook mark, badged.

FRAME E, the shared unsubscribe page.

LEGEND, six notes at most, among them: the three columns (pieces, the piece being written, the email as members get it); the cover and what the leaders supply each month; the no-photo cover; an empty piece is left out; the send rule (open for K); the address slot in the email footer and its setting.

boards.title: Newsletter · C · The month, built from the site
boards.name: Newsletter-C · The month, built from the site
boards.idea: The issue builds itself from what the site already holds, and the leaders only add their words on top. Coming up is filled from the calendar, Results from finished events, From the clubs from club posts, and the top stories from News. The page is a short checklist of those blocks, each showing what the site has put in it, with a box at the top for a note. If nobody touches it, it still goes out complete on the 1st.
boards.differs: The least work each month and the only one that can never go out late, empty or stale, which is the plainest reading of K's "goes out automatically ... unless edited". It looks like the site's own lists, so it has the least voice of the four, and what goes out is only as good as what clubs and directors have put on the site.
boards.keeps: First round, so nothing is carried over from an earlier option. From the decided boards: the signed-in header of Nav-Header-Final, the admin chrome of Work-J, the kit's k-* classes, the cream ground and navy bands, News-Final's dated rows and club colour dots wherever this spec names them, the phone chrome of Home-Final-Phones for the phone bezels, and the board furniture (title strip, legend, grey note).
boards.removes: Nothing: this is the first round for the newsletter. Do not draw the public News page, the preferences page in full, or Group email.
boards.spec:
BOARDS. Newsletter-C.dc.html, 1440 wide, under 3400. Newsletter-C-2.dc.html, 1440 wide, under 3000.

FRAME A, creating. Under the header and the crumb, a page heading "Newsletter" and, full width under it, a calm banner in words: "December 2026 will go out as it stands on Tue, Dec 1, 2026 at 8:00 AM Central, in 8 days. You do not have to do anything." with two buttons, "Hold this issue" and "Send a test to me". Below, two columns. LEFT, about 820px, "What is in it": six block cards stacked, each with a heading, a tag in words saying where it comes from, a switch drawn with its word ("Included" or "Left out"), a two or three line summary of what the site has put in it, and "Change". In order: (1) "A note from LCA", tag "Written by you": a writing box holding the president's note cut to two short paragraphs, "Last edited by President, Fri, Nov 20, 2026, 9:12 AM · History", and the line "Optional. The issue goes out without a note if this is empty." (2) "Coming up", tag "From the calendar": "4 events between Tue, Dec 1, 2026 and Sun, Jan 31, 2027", then the four as compact dated rows with weekdays, the partner event marked "Partner event · Registers on the organizer's site ↗"; drawn opened with "Change", so each row has a tick box and the last has "Add a line of your own". (3) "Results since last month", tag "From finished events": "1 event: the 2026 Louisiana State Championship" with the winners line; Included. (4) "From the clubs", tag "From club pages": "3 posts" with colour dots; Included. (5) "News you may have missed", tag "From News": "3 stories"; Included. (6) "Board business", tag "Written by you": empty, "Left out", with "Write something". Above the cards one line: "The site fills the lists again on the morning it is sent, so a result posted next week is included." RIGHT, about 480px: "What members will get", the email drawn live at reduced scale with the preview switch (Computer · Phone · Dark); under it the People card and the Goes to card.

THE SEND RULE for this option: it goes out by itself. The banner above is the rule. "Hold this issue" stops this month only and shows "Held by Media manager, Mon, Nov 23, 2026, 2:15 PM · Nothing will be sent until someone lets it go"; a guard line under the banner reads "If the site has nothing for a month (no events, no results, no posts and no note), nothing is sent and the three editors are told."

FRAME B, managing. (1) "What changed since you last looked": a short dated feed in words of what the site did on its own: "Sat, Nov 21, 2026: a club post was added to From the clubs (Bunkie Chess Club)", "Fri, Nov 20, 2026: President wrote the note", "Mon, Nov 16, 2026: December issue started by itself after November went out". (2) The banner in three states, in words: Going out as it stands, Held, Sent. (3) The report on November 2026. (4) Past issues as rows, each saying what it held in words and figures ("November 2026 · Sent Mon, Nov 16, 2026 · 5 events, 2 results, 4 club posts, a note from the president", Sample data). (5) Settings, with the mailing address "Not set", plus one more row here: "Blocks and their order", a small list with handles.

FRAME C, received on a computer. Subject "LCA Newsletter · December 2026 · 4 events, 1 result, 3 club posts". The inbox line, then the email: "Read this issue on the site", the title "The month in Louisiana chess" with "December 2026", the note in a tinted panel signed "LCA President", then each block under a navy rule and a heading as compact rows: Coming up (date with weekday, name, city, and either a Register link or "Registers on the organizer's site ↗"), Results (headline, winners line, "Full results"), From the clubs (colour dot, club, headline, "Club page"), News you may have missed (three dated lines). Each block ends with one link to its page on the site. Then the shared footer. Rows, not cards; no photos.

FRAME D, phones. Phone 1: the top of the email. Phone 2: the end with the footer, dark.

FRAME E, the shared unsubscribe page.

LEGEND, six notes at most, among them: which blocks fill themselves and from where; the note is the only part someone writes, and the issue goes out without it; the send rule: it goes out by itself, with Hold and the nothing-to-send guard (open for K); the feed of what the site changed; partner events never get Register; the address slot in the email footer and its setting.

boards.title: Newsletter · D · The bulletin, with chess in it
boards.name: Newsletter-D · The bulletin, with chess in it
boards.idea: A front page with a masthead, and chess on it. The leaders fill the places on a front page: a lead story, Dates to know, shorter pieces, and two things the other options do not have, a Position of the month to solve and a short item of Louisiana chess history. The page where it is made is the front page itself: click a place on it and write. The first position is Paul Morphy's, a New Orleans player, from Paris in 1858.
boards.differs: The only option that gives members a reason to open it beyond news: something to solve and something to learn every month. It has the strongest identity of the four and the most to prepare, because someone has to choose a position and a history item each month (a year of them can be prepared ahead and queued).
boards.keeps: First round, so nothing is carried over from an earlier option. From the decided boards: the signed-in header of Nav-Header-Final, the admin chrome of Work-J, the kit's k-* classes, the cream ground and navy bands, News-Final's dated rows and club colour dots wherever this spec names them, the phone chrome of Home-Final-Phones for the phone bezels, and the board furniture (title strip, legend, grey note).
boards.removes: Nothing: this is the first round for the newsletter. Do not draw the public News page, the preferences page in full, or Group email.
boards.spec:
BOARDS. Newsletter-D.dc.html, 1440 wide, under 3400. Newsletter-D-2.dc.html, 1440 wide, under 3000.

FRAME A, creating. Under the header and the crumb, a page heading "Newsletter" with the status line. Three parts. LEFT, about 260px, "Places on the page": a checklist, each place with its state in words: "Lead story · Written", "Dates to know · 4 chosen", "Position of the month · Chosen", "Results · Written", "From the clubs · President is editing" (with a lock), "From the archive · Not written yet", "Scholastic · Written", "Board business · Empty, will be left out". Under it the line "3 positions are queued for January to March 2027" with a link "Open the queue". CENTRE, about 700px: the front page itself, drawn at reduced scale as the email will look, every place outlined softly so it reads as a thing to click. At its top the masthead between a thick and a thin navy rule: the name set large in the kit's heading face, "Louisiana Chess Bulletin" (a working name; badge it and list it as open for K, with "LCA Newsletter" as the plain fallback), and under it in small capitals "Vol. 1 · No. 2 · December 2026 · Louisiana Chess Association · Since 1915". Then the lead story "Thank you, Sulphur" (the president's note as a front-page lead with a short standfirst and the hall photo), "Dates to know" as a boxed list of four dated lines, "Position of the month", "Results", "From the clubs", "From the archive", "Scholastic". The Position of the month place is the selected one: it has a navy outline and a numbered badge. RIGHT, about 400px: the side panel for the selected place, headed "Position of the month". In it: a board about 260px square showing the position; a field "Paste a position (FEN)" holding 4kb1r/p2n1ppp/4q3/4p1B1/4P3/1Q6/PPP2PPP/2KR4 w k - 1 16, with the words "or set the pieces on the board"; "Who moves" with White chosen; "Title" holding "Morphy at the opera"; "Line under the board" holding "White to move and mate in two. Paul Morphy, born in New Orleans, against the Duke of Brunswick and Count Isouard, Paris, 1858."; "The answer", drawn as a filled field whose text is covered by dots, with the words "Kept back. It is printed in the January issue as last month's answer."; and a read-only box "Text for people who cannot see the board, written for you" holding the piece list in words. Under the three parts, a slim strip with the status and schedule card, the People card and the Goes to card.

THE POSITION, to be placed exactly on every board that shows it (rank 8 at the top, file a at the left, a1 a dark square): White king c1, queen b3, rook d1, bishop g5, pawns a2, b2, c2, e4, f2, g2, h2. Black king e8, queen e6, rook h8, bishop f8, knight d7, pawns a7, e5, f7, g7, h7. Every other square is empty. Use the kit's cream for light squares and a soft navy tint for dark squares, with coordinates, and piece drawings copied from the scanner boards (see Scan-H.dc.html under docs/redesign/canvas/boards; if they cannot be reused, use the chess piece characters at a large size). The piece list in words, exactly as above, appears as real text wherever the board is shown to a reader. Do NOT print this month's answer anywhere on the boards or in the notes.

THE SEND RULE for this option: someone must say it is ready, and the checklist guards it. The status card shows "Mark as ready to send" and: "It goes out on Tue, Dec 1, 2026 at 8:00 AM Central once someone marks it ready. Places left empty are left out. If it is not ready the day before, the three editors get a reminder on Mon, Nov 30, 2026 at 8:00 AM. If it is still not ready, it waits and nothing is sent."

FRAME B, managing. (1) A second state of the side panel: "Dates to know" selected, where events are ticked from the site's calendar (four ticked, weekday first, the partner event marked "Partner event" with "Registers on the organizer's site ↗"). (2) "The queue": positions and archive items prepared ahead, three rows for January to March 2027 with a small board thumbnail each (plain empty boards with a Sample data badge; do not invent positions) and "Use this month". (3) The status card in the states Draft, Ready and Sent, in words. (4) The report on November 2026. (5) Past issues by volume: "Vol. 1 · No. 2 · December 2026 · Draft", "Vol. 1 · No. 1 · November 2026 · Sent Mon, Nov 16, 2026". (6) Settings, with the mailing address "Not set".

FRAME C, received on a computer. Subject "Louisiana Chess Bulletin · December 2026 · Can you find Morphy's mate in two?". The inbox line, then the email: "Read this issue on the site", the masthead with its volume line, the lead story with its standfirst and photo signed "LCA President", "Dates to know" as a boxed list (the LCA event with a Register link, the partner event with "Registers on the organizer's site ↗"), then "Position of the month" with the board as one picture, the title, the line under the board, the piece list in words as real text, "Answer in the January issue" and a small tinted strip "Last month's answer" with one line of Sample data; then Results, From the clubs with colour dots, "From the archive: 1858" and Scholastic, then the shared footer. From the archive reads: "The game above was played in a box at the Paris opera while the performance went on. Morphy, 21 and from New Orleans, was the strongest player in the world at the time. LCA has served Louisiana's chess community since 1915." No other historical claims.

FRAME D, phones. Phone 1: the masthead and the lead in the mail app. Phone 2: the Position of the month on a phone, board full width with the piece list under it, drawn dark, with the footer if it fits.

FRAME E, the shared unsubscribe page.

LEGEND, six notes at most, among them: the front page is the editor, click a place to write it; the masthead and the working name (open for K); the Position of the month: paste or set a position, the answer is kept back, and the text version is written for you; the queue prepared ahead; the send rule (open for K); the address slot in the email footer and its setting.

note: Written before K's decision of Tue, Nov 10, 2026 that no email carries a postal address. Where the flow or a spec speaks of a mailing address slot or setting, the boards as published have none: see the README's "Fixed before publishing".
